name: Path Solver
description: Automatically finds an input sequence that clears a level, with the game itself as the verifier.

issues.info: Report problems on the GitHub issue tracker.

play-menu.name: Choose the mode on Play
play-menu.description: Clicking a level's play button opens a menu: Normal, Replay or Solve. Off, a click just plays the level, as without the mod, and holding the play button opens the menu instead.

key-overlay.name: Hide the overlay
key-overlay.description: Refused while solving, and it never hides the bot badge.

key-render.name: Rendering on / off
key-render.description: Only during a solve, where the frames go back to the fast loop. A replay you cannot see is not a replay.

key-seek-back.name: Seek back
key-seek-back.description: A frame step instead while the game is stopped. Refused during a solve.

key-seek-forward.name: Seek forward
key-seek-forward.description: A frame step instead while the game is stopped. Refused during a solve.

key-takeover-end.name: End the human takeover
key-takeover-end.description: Debugging: ends a takeover session started with cfg takeover= and closes its records.

key-replaypanel.name: The replay panel
key-replaypanel.description: Shows GD's own record of the deepest verified attempt in the free corner of the screen, on and off.

human-min-click.name: Human style: minimum click length (ticks)
human-min-click.description: 0 = off. The solver will not change the button within this many ticks of the last change (240 ticks = 1 second), which removes taps no hand could place. 6 is about 25 ms. If a level needs a tighter tap the solver drops this limit and says so in the log. Needs a new solve to take effect.

portal-margin.name: No portal skips: margin (px)
portal-margin.description: Used when Avoid glitches is on (Solve > Options). A route that passes a portal which would change gamemode, size, gravity, speed or dual closer than this without touching it is dropped, so the solver goes through the portal as the level intends. 15 is the standard value; raise it (for example 60 or 120) if you still see a portal skipped. Where no route exists with it, the solver eases it for that stretch and says so. Needs a new solve.

wave-min-hold.name: Wave: minimum hold (ticks)
wave-min-hold.description: With Avoid glitches on its wave choice: the wave keeps each press or release at least this long (240 ticks = 1 second). 12 is standard. Raise it (18-24) for bigger, slower zigzags; where a corridor is too tight for that the solver eases it for that stretch and says so. Needs a new solve.

wave-click-cost.name: Wave: prefer fewer clicks (strength)
wave-click-cost.description: How strongly the solver prefers a wave route with fewer button changes. 4 is standard; 12-20 makes it take the longest diagonals a corridor allows. It only ranks routes, it never blocks one.

wave-centre-pull.name: Wave: stay near the middle (strength)
wave-centre-pull.description: How strongly the wave is pulled to the middle of its corridor. 8 is standard. Lower it (2-4) if the wave makes many small zigzags around the middle instead of a few big ones. It only ranks routes.

wave-slide.name: Wave: allow sliding on D-blocks
wave-slide.description: With Avoid glitches on its wave choice the wave is kept away from blocks. On, a wave resting on a block it can slide along (a D-block) is allowed, so it can slide through a low corridor instead of spamming. Needs a new solve.

wave-clearance.name: Wave: distance kept from blocks (px)
wave-clearance.description: With Avoid glitches on its wave choice: how far the wave stays from the floor, the ceiling and blocks. 10 is standard. Lower it (4-6) if a low corridor makes the solver give up the wave rules and spam; 0 turns the distance rule off.
